## 1.3.58 (HexGhoul): brothers and sisters play hide and seek (testing)
HexKagune 1.3.58 for Forge 1.20.1. Install on client and server (**protocol 70**, unchanged). Testing build: compiled, tests pass, **not tried in game**.

The owner liked the idea. When two siblings at home would play tag by day, half the time they play hide and seek instead:

- **"Hide and seek! I'll count!"** The one who suggests it counts, turned away with both hands over its eyes ("One... two... three...", a mischievous one: "One... two... *peeks* ...three..."), for five seconds, then "...ten! Ready or not, here I come!"
- **The other hides.** While the count goes on it runs to the best spot in the yard: it weighs up 24 places with ground to stand on and picks one the seeker can't see from where it counts (a real line-of-sight check: a block between them), the farther the better, and crouches down small there with its arms round its knees, peeking out. It never hides outside the yard.
- **The seeker looks about the yard**, wandering from spot to spot ("Hmm... where are you~?", "Come out, come out, wherever you are!"). Now and then the hider can't help a giggle (a thought cloud: "*tries very hard not to giggle*"), and if the seeker hears one it heads straight there.
- **Found:** within three blocks and in sight, "Found you!" (pointing), then the hider stands up: "Aww! No fair!", "You peeked! I KNOW you peeked!" (mischievous), "...you found me." (shy). **Not found** within 45 seconds: "Okay, I give up! Where are you?", and the hider pops out and runs over: "*pops out* Boo! I win!", "I was right behind you the WHOLE time."
- Two new poses for it: crouched down hiding, and hands over the eyes for counting (a toddler's short arms only reach its cheeks, so it bows its big head into its hands). 80 lines in all, by temper and age (toddlers count "One, two, free, four...").
- **It stops cleanly** when one of them is hurt, fights, falls asleep, is picked up, starts a talk, is told to follow, or a player talks to one of them; a player's hug or other moment ends the game, while a parent's cuddle waits until it is over. A hiding child isn't picked up for a cuddle.

Untested in game: compiled and unit tested only. Try: two children at home by day, and wait for a game.
